shape_hint: A headless double-ended threaded rod: a short fully-threaded tap end (about 1.5 D, interference-fit class 5) screwed into the casing, then a plain unthreaded body of reduced or full diameter, then a longer nut end with full thread (B) where a heavy hex nut is fitted; both ends have a chamfered lead-in (U).

role_map.Bm: nominal full thread length of tap end (1.5 D)
role_map.Umax: max length from stud end to first full-form thread (=2 pitches, UNC)
role_map.B_le10: min full-thread length at nut end for stud length L<=10 in
role_map.B_10_16: min full-thread length at nut end for 10<L<=16 in
role_map.B_gt16: min full-thread length at nut end for L>16 in

notes: Tap-end (interference fit, ASME B1.12 Class 5/NC-5) stud: B is nut-end full thread; stud overall length L is customer specified; stand-off S = L - Bm. Table 3 of B18.31.2 applies to 1.5D engagement; other engagement tables (1D, 2D) were not checked. Sizes 3, 3-1/4, 3-1/2, 3-3/4, 4 in exist with only B(10<L<=16) and B(L>16) and Bm (Bm 4.5/4.875/5.25/5.625/6.0 on bp,fasten.it,nickel; B(L>16) 7/7.5/8/8.5/9) - kept out of the table only because of the no-empty-cell rule for B(L<=10). Thread = UNC (NC-5) tap end; UNF/8UN variants not tabulated. Sizes 1-5/8 and 1-7/8 are 8UN-only.

problems: Every kept cell is supported by exactly 3 clusters (Bm and B columns: Boltport, fasten.it, Nickel Systems; Umax: Boltport, Nickel, TorqBolt). Zero margin.

Independence risk: Nickel Systems' tap-end table has different headings, no Bm min/max and only UNC/UNF Umax columns, and different typos ('11/2') than Boltport ('1.1.25') -> counted as an independent transcription of the standard. If a reviewer judges Nickel to be derived from Boltport, Bm and B columns drop to 2 clusters on ALL rows and the record fails.
aesteiron.com cannot be re-fetched (captcha); its rows are in scrambled order (looks like a reshuffled copy). Not used to reach 3.
TorqBolt's table is the continuous-thread stud table (U min/max, Table 1), not the tap-end table; U values are the same 2P numbers, used only for Umax.
